title: Latin Prose Style and Rhetoric
objectives: Identify rhetorical devices in Latin prose

grammar.explanation: Roman orators employed sophisticated rhetorical techniques. Understanding these enhances both comprehension and appreciation of Latin prose.

readingPassage.latin: Nihilne te nocturnum praesidium Palati, nihil urbis vigiliae, nihil timor populi, nihil concursus bonorum omnium, nihil hic munitissimus habendi senatus locus, nihil horum ora voltusque moverunt?
readingPassage.translation: Did the nocturnal guard of the Palatine not move you at all, nor the city watches, nor the fear of the people, nor the gathering of all good citizens, nor this most fortified place for holding the senate, nor the faces and expressions of these men?
readingPassage.analysis: Sixfold anaphora of 'nihil' builds overwhelming rhetorical force. Climax moves from abstract (guard, fear) to concrete (faces).

exercises.question: Identify the rhetorical devices in: 'abiit, excessit, evasit, erupit'
exercises.answer: Asyndeton (no conjunctions), Climax (increasing intensity), Tetracolon (four parallel verbs)
